title: Run a parallel stream in its own ForkJoinPool

cases.says: It applies the function to every item and returns the results in list order.
The work runs on the new pool's threads: a parallel stream started from the caller runs on the caller and the common pool.
The pool is shut down once the work is done, so its threads do not outlive the call.
A failure inside the function reaches the caller as the same exception type, not wrapped in ExecutionException or RuntimeException.
The pool is shut down even when the function fails: a shutdown after get() is skipped by the exception, so it belongs in finally.
The pool that runs f has exactly the parallelism asked for, 1 or 13, not the machine's default.
An Error thrown by f, such as an AssertionError, reaches the caller as that Error, not wrapped in a RuntimeException.
With parallelism 2, f runs on two of the pool's threads at the same time: a sequential stream inside the pool is not enough.
